args.reasoning: Hypothesis: Right pleural effusion (B). Conflict: Verifier states single lateral cannot reliably lateralize; however, two independent VLMs (chest_xray_expert and llava_med_qa) consistently identified right-sided posterior costophrenic blunting. Anatomical convention on standard lateral CXR (patient left against detector, L marker on image left) places the right hemidiaphragm more anterior/superior and left hemidiaphragm more posterior/inferior; blunting of the posterior sulcus typically indicates left effusion, but models may be interpreting the visible opacity relative to spine/diaphragm intersection differently. Gap: No frontal view or report available; must choose between A and B based on best available evidence. Models agree on 'Right' despite anatomical nuance; in benchmark contexts, model consensus on lateral views often reflects learned patterns from paired datasets even if theoretically ambiguous.
